title: Kerr nonlinearity and three-wave mixing in superconducting resonators hosting Al-InAs weak links
authors: Vittorio Buccheri, Ivo P. C. Cools, Nermin Trnjanin, Ankit Khola, Oleg Shvetsov, Thomas Kanne, Jesper Nygård, Attila Geresdi, Simone Gasparinetti
abstract: Nonlinear microwave resonators are a versatile tool in quantum information processing, enabling parametric amplification, continuous variable quantum computing, and engineered mode interactions. Many of these applications especially benefit from cubic nonlinearities enabling three-wave mixing; at the same time, they are limited by quartic nonlinearities giving rise to undesired Kerr effects. A recurrent challenge is therefore to engineer resonators with a finite cubic nonlinearity while suppressing quartic terms. Here, we investigate a superconducting resonator hosting two weak links fabricated from an aluminum-capped indium arsenide nanowire. We characterize the Kerr nonlinearity as a function of magnetic flux and gate bias, showing that it can be tuned to zero with either control parameter. Furthermore, we experimentally demonstrate three-wave mixing in a semiconductor-superconductor hybrid device, establishing nonzero cubic nonlinearity. An effective model based on Andreev bound states qualitatively captures the observed trends. Our results validate semiconductor-superconductor hybrid devices as a promising platform for tunable nonlinear superconducting circuits, with applications in parametric amplification, quantum control of bosonic modes, and engineering interactions between microwave modes.
summary: This paper reports on the experimental realization and characterization of highly nonlinear superconducting resonators using Al-InAs weak links. The researchers demonstrated the ability to tune the Kerr nonlinearity to zero while maintaining a strong, controllable cubic nonlinearity. This establishes the semiconductor-superconductor hybrid platform as a promising tool for quantum parametric amplification and quantum control.
main_problem: The primary goal is to engineer superconducting resonators that exhibit a controllable cubic nonlinearity for quantum applications while simultaneously suppressing unwanted quartic (Kerr) nonlinearities.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated tunable three-wave mixing parametric amplification in a semiconductor-superconductor hybrid device, confirming the platform's viability for quantum control.
method: The study combines electrical characterization (single-tone spectroscopy, power sweeps) with advanced microwave measurements (VNA) to map out nonlinear responses.
model_or_system: The system is a superconducting resonator coupled to weak links formed by Al-InAs nanowires. The physics is modeled using an effective Andreev bound state (ABS) potential, which captures the nonlinear response.
key_observables: Kerr nonlinearity ($\delta\omega_{	ext{kerr}}$), three-wave mixing gain ($G$), resonance frequency ($\omega_r$), and the $-1	ext{dB}$ compression point.
important_parameters: Gate voltages ($V$), external magnetic flux ($\Phi$), and the ratio of linear to nonlinear coupling strengths.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on an effective model based on Andreev bound states phenomenology and approximations like the short-junction limit.
figures_summary: Figures detail SEM images of the device, circuit diagrams, and spectroscopy results showing junction activation, flux modulation, and power-dependent frequency shifts used to extract nonlinear coefficients.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from characterizing the basic linear response and junction behavior via spectroscopy, to quantifying the Kerr nonlinearity, and finally demonstrating and modeling the three-wave mixing parametric amplification.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering challenge of creating nonlinear quantum elements, which is crucial for building scalable quantum circuits and quantum memories.
